passages.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years. His mother’s name was Hephzibah.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh became king when he was twelve years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem.
He ruled for fifty-five years.
His mother was Hephzibah.
passages.original: בֶּן־ שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֥ם אִמּ֖וֹ חֶפְצִי־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king in Jerusalem.
\r\nHe did evil.
\r\nThe LORD saw his evil.
\r\nManasseh followed the abominations of the nations.
\r\nThese nations had lived in the land before Israel.
\r\nThe LORD had driven out these nations before the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For he rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed, and he raised up altars for Baal. He made an Asherah pole, as King Ahab of Israel had done, and he worshiped and served all the host of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king in Jerusalem.
Hezekiah was his father.
Hezekiah had destroyed the high places.
Manasseh rebuilt the high places.
Manasseh set up altars for Baal.
Manasseh made an Asherah pole.
King Ahab of Israel had also made an Asherah pole.
Manasseh worshiped all the host of heaven.
Manasseh served all the host of heaven.
passages.original: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ אֶת־ הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִבַּ֖ד חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּחֹ֜ת לַבַּ֗עַל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֲשֵׁרָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ לְכָל־ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Manasseh also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem I will put My Name.”
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh built altars inside the house of the LORD.
The house of the LORD was the temple in Jerusalem.
The LORD had said, “In Jerusalem I will put My Name.”
The LORD chose Jerusalem for His Name to dwell there.
Manasseh built these altars in the very place God had chosen.
passages.original: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־ שְׁמִֽי׃

passages.text: In both courtyards of the house of the LORD, he built altars to all the host of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD.
He built altars to all the host of heaven.
He put these altars in both courtyards of the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל־ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He sacrificed his own son in the fire, practiced sorcery and divination, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh sacrificed his own son in the fire.
Manasseh practiced sorcery.
Manasseh practiced divination.
Manasseh consulted mediums.
Manasseh consulted spiritists.
Manasseh did great evil in the sight of the LORD.
Manasseh provoked the LORD to anger.
passages.original: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת־ בְּנוֹ֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעוֹנֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס׃

passages.text: Manasseh even took the carved Asherah pole he had made and set it up in the temple, of which the LORD had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh made a carved Asherah pole.
He took the Asherah pole he made.
He set up the Asherah pole in the temple.
The temple was the house of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to David and to Solomon, David’s son.
The LORD said about this temple and about Jerusalem, “I have chosen them from all the tribes of Israel.”
The LORD said, “I will put My Name there forever.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת־ פֶּ֥סֶל הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בַּבַּ֗יִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ דָּוִד֙ וְאֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֙רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: I will never again cause the feet of the Israelites to wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they are careful to do all I have commanded them—the whole Law that My servant Moses commanded them.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave land to the ancestors of the Israelites.
God promised not to make the Israelites leave this land again.
God required the Israelites to obey Him.
God commanded them to do everything He told them.
God gave them the whole Law through His servant Moses.
God said the Israelites must be careful to obey all these commands.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א אֹסִ֗יף לְהָנִיד֙ רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם רַ֣ק׀ אִם־ יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים וּלְכָל־ הַ֨תּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם עַבְדִּ֥י מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: But the people did not listen and Manasseh led them astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
The people did not listen.
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh led the people astray.
The people did more evil than the nations.
The LORD had destroyed those nations before the Israelites.
passages.original: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּתְעֵ֤ם מְנַשֶּׁה֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֶת־ הָרָ֔ע מִן־ הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And the LORD spoke through His servants the prophets, saying, “Since Manasseh king of Judah has committed all these abominations, acting more wickedly than the Amorites who preceded him, and with his idols has caused Judah to sin, this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I am bringing such calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah that the news will reverberate in the ears of all who hear it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke through His servants.
His servants are the prophets.
The LORD gave a message.
Manasseh is the king of Judah.
Manasseh committed many abominations.
Manasseh did more evil than the Amorites who lived before him.
Manasseh used idols.
Manasseh caused Judah to sin with his idols.
The LORD said this:
“I am bringing disaster on Jerusalem and Judah.
Everyone who hears about it will be shocked.
The news will make both ears of every listener tingle.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־ עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃ יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָה֙ הַתֹּעֵב֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה הֵרַ֕ע מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשׂ֥וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּחֲטִ֥א גַֽם־ אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּגִלּוּלָֽיו׃פ לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּל־ שֹׁמְעָיו תִּצַּ֖לְנָה שְׁתֵּ֥י אָזְנָֽיו׃

passages.text: I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measuring line used against Samaria and the plumb line used against the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes out a bowl—wiping it and turning it upside down.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will judge Jerusalem.
The LORD will use the same standard He used against Samaria.
The LORD will use the same measure He used against the house of Ahab.
The LORD will wipe out Jerusalem.
The LORD will wipe Jerusalem like a person wipes a bowl.
The LORD will wipe the bowl clean.
The LORD will turn the bowl upside down.
passages.original: וְנָטִ֣יתִי עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֵ֚ת קָ֣ו שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְאֶת־ מִשְׁקֹ֖לֶת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וּמָחִ֨יתִי אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ יִמְחֶ֤ה אֶת־ הַצַּלַּ֙חַת֙ מָחָ֔ה וְהָפַ֖ךְ עַל־ פָּנֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: So I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance and deliver them into the hands of their enemies. And they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies, because they have done evil in My sight and have provoked Me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about His people.
The LORD says He will abandon the remnant of His inheritance.
The LORD will give them into the hands of their enemies.
Their enemies will plunder them.
Their enemies will take them as spoil.
The LORD does this because His people have done evil in His sight.
They have provoked the LORD to anger.
They have done this from the day their fathers left Egypt.
They have continued to do this until this day.
passages.original: וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֗י אֵ֚ת שְׁאֵרִ֣ית נַחֲלָתִ֔י וּנְתַתִּ֖ים בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבַ֛ז וְלִמְשִׁסָּ֖ה לְכָל־ אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃ יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת־ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וַיִּהְי֥וּ מַכְעִסִ֖ים אֹתִ֑י מִן־ הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֤וּ אֲבוֹתָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Moreover, Manasseh shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from end to end, in addition to the sin that he had caused Judah to commit, doing evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh killed many innocent people.
He shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other.
This was not his only sin.
Manasseh also led Judah to sin.
He caused Judah to do evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.original: וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ מִלֵּ֥א אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם פֶּ֣ה לָפֶ֑ה לְבַ֤ד מֵֽחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, along with all his accomplishments and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
He did many things during his reign.
He also sinned greatly.
The rest of Manasseh’s deeds are recorded.
His accomplishments are written down.
His sins are also written down.
These records are in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְחַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried in his palace garden, the garden of Uzza. And his son Amon reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh died.
People buried Manasseh in the garden of his palace.
This garden was called the garden of Uzza.
Amon was Manasseh’s son.
Amon became king after Manasseh.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּגַן־ בֵּית֖וֹ בְּגַן־ עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem two years. His mother’s name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz; she was from Jotbah.
passages.sermon:
Amon became king when he was twenty-two years old.
Amon ruled in Jerusalem.
Amon ruled for two years.
Amon’s mother was Meshullemeth.
Meshullemeth was the daughter of Haruz.
Meshullemeth was from Jotbah.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מְשֻׁלֶּ֥מֶת בַּת־ חָר֖וּץ מִן־ יָטְבָֽה׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king in Jerusalem.
Amon did evil things.
The LORD saw Amon’s evil actions.
Amon acted like his father Manasseh.
Manasseh, Amon’s father, also did evil.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: He walked in all the ways of his father, and he served and worshiped the idols his father had served.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king in Jerusalem.
Amon’s father was Manasseh.
Amon acted like his father Manasseh.
Amon followed every way that his father had followed.
Amon served the same idols that his father had served.
Amon worshiped those idols.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל־ הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ הָלַ֣ךְ אָבִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־ הַגִּלֻּלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֣ד אָבִ֔יו וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: He abandoned the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king of Judah.
Amon left the LORD.
The LORD was the God of Amon’s ancestors.
Amon did not follow the LORD’s way.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲזֹ֕ב אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א הָלַ֖ךְ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the servants of Amon conspired against him and killed the king in his palace.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king of Judah.
Amon had servants.
The servants of Amon made a secret plan against him.
They conspired against Amon.
The servants killed Amon.
They killed him in his own palace.
passages.original: וַיִּקְשְׁר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־ אָמ֖וֹן עָלָ֑יו וַיָּמִ֥יתוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
passages.sermon:
The people of the land acted together.
They killed everyone who had conspired against King Amon.
King Amon was Josiah’s father.
The people of the land made Josiah king after Amon died.
Josiah became king in his father’s place.
passages.original: וַיַּךְ֙ עַם־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָמ֑וֹן וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם־ הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Amon, along with his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
Amon was king of Judah.
Amon did many things during his reign.
The Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah records these acts and accomplishments.
You can find the rest of what Amon did in that book.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And he was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Amon was king of Judah.
People buried Amon in his own tomb.
This tomb was in the garden of Uzza.
Josiah was Amon’s son.
Josiah became king after Amon died.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ר אֹת֛וֹ בִּקְבֻרָת֖וֹ בְּגַן־ עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
